title: Evaluation of the Anti-Plasmodial potential of Calotropis procera Latex in mice infected with Plasmodium berghei
author: Adejoh, Alli, et al.
materials: V1 = Initial volume of the stock;
V2 = Final volume of the diluted solution;

steps.title: Prepare 1 M phosphate buffer stock
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1 L stock solution of 1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.0) using the Henderson‑Hasselbalch equation with pKa = 6.9 and a base/acid ratio of 1.096.

substeps.instruction: Calculate acid concentration: 0.477 mol L⁻¹; calculate base concentration: 0.523 mol L⁻¹.
Weigh 57.24 g monosodium phosphate (NaH₂PO₄, M = 120 g mol⁻¹) and dissolve in less than 1 L distilled water.
Weigh 74.27 g disodium phosphate (Na₂HPO₄, M = 142 g mol⁻¹) and dissolve in less than 1 L distilled water.
Combine both solutions, check pH with a pH meter, and adjust to 7.0 with phosphoric acid or NaOH as needed.
Add distilled water to bring the total volume to exactly 1 L.

steps.title: Dilute stock to 0.2 M buffer
steps.instruction: Dilute the 1 M phosphate buffer stock to a 0.2 M solution (pH 7.0) using the dilution equation C₁V₁ = C₂V₂.

substeps.instruction: Identify C₁ (1 M), C₂ (0.2 M), and V₂ (desired final volume, e.g., 1 L).
Calculate the required volume of stock (V₁) with C₁V₁ = C₂V₂ and add distilled water to reach V₂.

steps.title: Extract latex with phosphate buffer
steps.instruction: Extract bioactive constituents from Calotropis procera latex using the prepared 0.2 M phosphate buffer.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 25 g of crude latex on an analytical balance.
Transfer the latex into a conical flask.
Measure 50 mL of the 0.2 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.0) and add to the flask; stir continuously for 20 min.
Filter the mixture through muslin cloth to remove cell debris.
Transfer the filtrate to test tubes and centrifuge in a Theodor Svedberg analytical centrifuge for 15 min at 10 000 rpm to obtain a clear filtrate.
Collect the clear filtrate in a beaker for subsequent acetone precipitation.

steps.title: Prepare Plasmodium berghei inoculum
steps.instruction: Generate a parasite inoculum and infect experimental mice.

substeps.instruction: Inoculate two donor mice (each 25 g) intraperitoneally with cultured Plasmodium berghei NK65 (chloroquine‑sensitive) and maintain for 5–8 days.
Determine each mouse’s parasitemia using % Parasitemia = (parasitized RBC / total RBC) × 100.
Select a donor mouse with ~20 % parasitemia, sacrifice, and draw blood into a heparinised syringe; dilute the blood with normal saline.
Inject 0.2 mL of the diluted parasite preparation intraperitoneally into each healthy recipient mouse.
Monitor infected mice by preparing Giemsa‑stained thin blood smears, counting parasitized erythrocytes in 5–10 fields twice, and averaging to obtain parasitemia for each mouse.

steps.title: Prepare Mayer's reagent
steps.instruction: Make Mayer’s reagent working solution (100 mL total).

substeps.instruction: Prepare Solution A: dissolve 1.358 g mercuric chloride in 60 mL distilled water.
Prepare Solution B: dissolve 5 g potassium iodide in 10 mL distilled water.
Combine Solutions A and B and add distilled water to reach a final volume of 100 mL.

steps.title: Prepare ferric chloride solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a ferric chloride solution using concentrated HCl as a medium.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 67.5 g ferric chloride and mix with 5 mL concentrated HCl to form a paste.
Slowly add distilled water to the paste until the solution reaches the calibration mark of the chosen volumetric flask.

steps.title: Prepare ammonia solution (1 L)
steps.instruction: Make a 1 L aqueous ammonia solution.

substeps.instruction: Measure 71.0 mL concentrated ammonia solution.
Transfer the measured ammonia to a 1 L volumetric flask.
Add distilled water up to the calibration mark.

steps.title: Prepare acetic acid solution (1 L)
steps.instruction: Make a 1 L aqueous acetic acid solution.

substeps.instruction: Measure 58.0 mL glacial acetic acid.
Transfer the measured acid to a 1 L volumetric flask.
Add distilled water up to the calibration mark.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze experimental data using JMP v.14 software.

substeps.instruction: Conduct one‑way ANOVA with Dunnett’s post‑test to compare treatment groups.
Consider results statistically significant when P < 0.05 for both mean parasitaemia count and mean mouse weight.
